newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA NEPTUN SAW H1 PROFIT SHARPLY DOWN.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA NEPTUN SAW H1 PROFIT SHARPLY DOWN.

text.p: Neptun SA, a Bucharest bourse listed state engineer, said its half-year gross profit had plummeted to 126.2 million lei from 3.4 billion due to costlier raw materials and high interest rates.

"The main reason behind the fall in our six-month profit was the high interest credits which we had to resort to due to financial bottlenecks," company manager Grigore Marinescu said on Friday from Cimpina, 70 km (43 miles) north of Bucharest.
He said bottlenecks had prevented Neptun end-users from paying bills on time, forcing the company to make credits to meet costs, wages included.
Lending rates at Romanian commercial banks average 60 percent.
According to Industry Ministry sources, payment arrears in the Romanian economy stand at around 18 trillion lei, almost the equivalent of the country's money supply.
Neptun also had big spending on raw materials, Marinescu said.
Neptun, a producer of helical gears, pump rotors and casing for gear units and pumps, planned a net profit in excess of 2.0 billion lei this year, from 1.7 billion in 1995.
Brokerage sources said the company might still attain its target helped by plans to upgrade its technology to boost exports, expected to take some 25 percent of the 1996 turnover.
Turnover this year is forecast at 48 billion lei, from 30 billion in 1995. ($=3,177 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
